steps.what: Read transportation schedules and production requirements before any move
Coordinate the selection and movement of logs from storage areas
Move those logs according to the schedule she chose

tasks.design: She still reads the transportation schedule and the production requirement, and she still selects and moves the logs with the crew. No list is copied and nothing is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Which logs leave the storage area depends on the schedule, the pile and the crew on the yard.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new pulls a log. The schedule can sit on a screen, and the selection stays hers.
tasks.still_hard: A log that looks right on the schedule can be the wrong length once she sees the pile.
tasks.human_edge: She sees the pile and the crew. The selection does not move to a list.
tasks.altitude: Selecting and moving the logs stays in her week. Nothing leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Lift and carry the log she selected
reach.learn: Which lengths and piles the machine can take without a second move

evidence.claim: Selecting logs and moving them with a crew is yard coordination. Model knowledge: a schedule does not choose the log.

assumptions: The crew is inside the yard. Telling them which log to take is not a send outside the organisation.
No load list already goes to an outside haulier in this task, so nothing is copied.
Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: How often an outside haulier is booked from this task rather than told on the yard.
research_questions: How often the transportation schedule names the exact logs, and how often she chooses them at the pile?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still selects the logs and still moves them with the crew. There is no list that already leaves the yard.

steps.what: Read the locations, crews and equipment already named
Schedule work crews, equipment or transportation for several different work locations
State the crew, the equipment, the transportation and the location
Copy that stated crew and location onto the schedule
Check the schedule names her crew, her equipment and her locations
Write the accepted schedule into the crew plan

tasks.design: She chooses the crew, the equipment and the transportation for each location, and she states those fields. A copy fills them on the {OTHER} crew plan and does not wait. She checks the crew, the equipment and the locations, and only the accepted schedule is written. A rejection writes nothing. The plan stores no pace and does not rank anyone.
tasks.previous_blocker: The week's locations lived in her head or on a note, and the crew heard them one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: A crew plan can hold a named person, a piece of equipment and a location once she states them. Model knowledge.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to know who can do the location. A copied name does not make a crew fit.
tasks.human_edge: She knows who is able and which location clashes. The plan only holds what she states.
tasks.altitude: Choosing who goes where stays in her week. Only typing the accepted schedule leaves it. She gains no right to skip that choice.

reach.learn: How long that location actually takes, so the next schedule is not only a name

evidence.claim: A crew plan can store a person, a piece of equipment and a location once the supervisor states them. Model knowledge: it does not choose the crew.

Transportation here is the yard's own equipment. An outside haulier is not booked.

A rejected line is dropped in the check, so her upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: Whether posting names and locations on this yard already has works-council consent.

tasks.short: Supervise, and do the management work.

steps.what: Perform the supervisory functions with the crew on the floor
Do the management functions such as accounting, marketing and personnel work

tasks.design: She still directs the crew and still does the accounting, marketing and personnel judgements. No letter is drafted and no score is kept. The week keeps the whole job.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directing the crew and judging a personnel matter are the same person on the same day, and neither is a form.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new takes the direction or the personnel decision. A generated letter would still need her decision first.
tasks.still_hard: Accounting, marketing and a disciplinary point do not share a rule she could hand to a copy.
tasks.human_edge: She knows the person and the day. A note cannot make the personnel decision.
tasks.altitude: Directing the crew and the personnel judgement stay in her week. Nothing leaves it. She gains no new decision right.

reach.task: Follow the direction she gave on the shift
reach.learn: Which instructions the crew can carry out without her standing there

evidence.claim: Directing a crew and deciding a personnel matter stay with the supervisor. Model knowledge: a letter draft would not remove either.
Promotion or disciplinary decisions may not rest solely on automated processing.

assumptions: Personnel, accounting and marketing judgements stay with her. No letter is drafted from this task.
No pace score is kept.
Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: How often this task is a written personnel letter rather than direction on the floor.
research_questions: Which of accounting, marketing and personnel work she actually does in a normal week, and which sit with another role?

incremental.description: Nothing is built, so upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: She still directs the crew and still makes the accounting, marketing and personnel judgements. No letter is added for a machine to draft.

steps.what: Copy inventory records, customer orders and shipping schedules into one list
Check the list keeps her order lines and the quantities
Determine the required activities from the orders she kept

tasks.design: Structured inventory, customer orders and shipping dates already on the {OTHER} order platform are copied into one list. She checks the lines and the quantities. A line with no article code or no quantity is not copied, and she reads that order herself. She still determines the required activities. The list is not sent to a customer, and it does not choose the work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders, stock and shipping dates sat in separate notes, and she lined them up before she could say what the day required.
tasks.enabler_now: An order platform can hold stock and orders and can offer them to other software. Model knowledge: code can list lines that already have an article code and a quantity.
tasks.still_hard: A matching line is not the activity. She still has to say what the crew does, and a free-text order still needs her.
tasks.human_edge: She decides the activities. The list only gathers lines she can already point at.
tasks.altitude: Determining the required activities stays in her week. Only collating structured orders, stock and shipping dates leaves it. She gains no right to skip a mismatch.

reach.task: Enter the customer order with an article code and a quantity
reach.learn: Which order fields must be present before a line can be copied

evidence.claim: A horticulture order platform lets growers manage stock and orders across sales channels, and offers an API for other software.
Code can list structured order lines and quantities into one daily list. Model knowledge: the supervisor still settles a mismatch and still determines the activities.

assumptions: Inventory, customer orders and shipping dates already exist as structured records. She does not create them in this task.

Try the order platform's own list before custom code. Existing screen time is not her effort.
The copy does not rephrase a line and does not decide the activity.
The list is for her. It is not sent to a customer and it is not released to the crew as an order.
No model reads the order.
Sales owns the feed. A mismatch is handled in the check, so her upkeep hours are zero.
unknowns: How often orders on this yard are structured lines, and how often they are still free-text mail.
research_questions: Which share of customer orders already carries an article code and a quantity?

already_counted.description: The check that the list keeps her order lines and quantities, already counted in the review step.

incremental.description: Sales owns the order feed. A mismatch is handled in the check, so her upkeep hours are zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most orders still arrive as free text with no article code, so she still reads them and the copy rarely runs. High: most orders and stock records are already structured, and only the collating leaves. She still determines the activities.
